name: Derrick May
hook: The second of the Belleville Three, whose "Strings of Life" is the record most often used to explain techno's emotional range.

blurb.age7: Derrick May made electronic music with real feeling in it, not just machine sounds, and his friends called him techno's "Innovator."
blurb.age13: May grew up in Belleville, Michigan with Juan Atkins and Kevin Saunderson, and the three of them are called the Belleville Three for starting Detroit techno together. Recording as Rhythim Is Rhythim, May's 1987 track "Strings of Life" used string-like synth sounds to make electronic music feel warm instead of cold, on his own label, Transmat.
blurb.adult: May is usually cast as techno's emotional counterweight to Atkins' conceptual rigor: "Strings of Life," released on his own Transmat in 1987, took the genre's machine palette and pushed it toward the euphoric, string-drenched sound that helped drive the UK's 1987-88 house explosion. Transmat also became a launching label for later Detroit and Chicago-adjacent producers.

signatureTracks.title: Strings of Life (Rhythim Is Rhythim)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Synthetic string stabs over a stripped drum pattern; the record most credited with giving techno an emotional register beyond function.

signatureTracks.title: Nude Photo (Rhythim Is Rhythim)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Transmat's first release, and a harder, more functional counterpart to "Strings of Life" from the same sessions.
